paper_metadata.title: H-EFT-VA: An Effective-Field-Theory Variational Ansatz with Provable Barren Plateau Avoidance

summary: The paper proposes the H‑EFT‑VA variational ansatz with small‑scale EFT‑inspired parameter initialization and proves an inverse‑polynomial gradient variance bound Var[∂θ] ∈ Ω(1/poly(N)). In simulations up to 14 qubits on TFIM and Heisenberg XXZ Hamiltonians, it achieves a final energy of −12.00 vs −0.11 for a hardware‑efficient ansatz (reported 109× improvement), ground‑state fidelity 0.2646 vs 0.0247 (10.7× higher), and maintains gradient variance ≈10⁻⁵ at N=14 while the baseline collapses to ~10⁻¹⁶.

experiments.description: Benchmarking the proposed H-EFT variational ansatz against a hardware-efficient ansatz on noiseless and depolarizing-noise simulations for TFIM and Heisenberg XXZ ground-state optimization, including gradient-variance scaling, convergence, noise robustness, entanglement, purity, fidelity, and parameter-efficiency tests.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Gaussian prior with small-scale hierarchical initialization; parameters initialized as coupling constants with sigma = kappa/(L·N), and in appendix as theta = alpha * c with alpha ~ N(0, sigma_init^2), sigma_init << 1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Variational ground-state preparation for local Hamiltonians (TFIM and Heisenberg XXZ); no explicit binary-variable encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize expectation value of the Hamiltonian C(θ)=⟨ψ(θ)|H|ψ(θ)⟩
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Transverse Field Ising Model and Heisenberg XXZ Hamiltonians

problem_instance.description: Ground-state optimization benchmarks on TFIM and Heisenberg XXZ models across multiple qubit counts and circuit depths

dataset_specification.description: Hamiltonian benchmark instances; system sizes N=4,6,8,12,14 and depths L=2,4,6,8,10,12,14

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Multiple benchmark tests (16 total) including gradient-variance scaling, energy landscape scans, convergence trajectories, noise robustness, finite-shot robustness, entanglement/purity, fidelity, and parameter-efficiency comparisons against HEA; statistical significance reported with p-values

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: H-EFT-VA converges smoothly to lower energies than HEA; HEA stagnates for N≥8

speedup_claims.conditions: ground-state energy convergence benchmark at N=12
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as final energy -12.00 vs -0.11; this is a performance ratio on a specific benchmark, not a proven asymptotic speedup.
Based on fidelity 0.2646 vs 0.0247; benchmark-specific and not a general complexity result.
A proof claim for the ansatz initialization regime; does not imply overall optimization speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly stated; variational circuit cost and gradient variance discussed, with inverse-polynomial gradient variance lower bound

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown; experiments only simulate up to N=14 qubits and compare two quantum ansätze within VQE rather than quantum vs classical solvers.
limiting_factors: All results obtained via classical simulation (PennyLane) up to 14 qubits
No comparison against classical ground‑state solvers (e.g., exact diagonalization, tensor networks)
Performance improvement is relative to another quantum ansatz (HEA) rather than classical methods
No asymptotic runtime or complexity advantage demonstrated

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_noisy because the paper reports PennyLane simulations with depolarizing noise and finite shots, but no real QPU device is named.
num_qubits and circuit_depth taken as the maximum reported benchmark size (N=14, L=14) from the experiments and figures.
The paper does not report transpiled depth, gate counts, or specific gate fidelities.
The paper compares against a classical optimizer baseline (HEA) but does not provide a classical asymptotic complexity or a proven quantum speedup order.
The paper reports improvements (109× lower final energy error and 10.7× higher fidelity) relative to a hardware‑efficient ansatz baseline.
However, this is an ansatz comparison within VQE and not a quantum vs classical benchmark; therefore quantum advantage cannot be evaluated under the Hoefler framework.
